intent.purpose: BE the harness in document form. A single, large, consolidated JSON file that any Claude Code agent loads into context and uses to BEHAVE as if the ideal harness was fully implemented. This means the agent can: make governance decisions (from GOVERNANCE), modify and extend code correctly (from IMPLEMENTATION), assess the current state of all work streams (from STATE), and avoid repeating mistakes (from OPERATIONAL LEARNING). When loaded alongside the rules and CLAUDE.md that CC injects, the agent has the FULL harness.
intent.scope: Everything the harness IS and aspires to be, organized into FOUR PILLARS: Governance (what was decided), Implementation (what was built), State (where things are), Operational Learning (what was learned). NOT a copy of source files. NOT static — it is an assumption the moment written.
intent.audience: Any and all Claude Code agents. Loaded into context at session start. Used to behave, not just to know.

meta.label: Governance
meta.description: What was decided — all governance artifacts for the aitools harness: design principles, rules, skills, frameworks, standing orders, and key decisions.

design_principles.label: Three-layer governance
design_principles.statement: Prevention (rules in context stop issues from being created), Detection (hooks fire in real-time during sessions), Audit (skills/subagents provide deep review on demand). Each layer catches what the previous missed.
design_principles.evidence: All 3 layers active: 23 rules in context (prevention), 11 hooks deployed (detection), audit/incident/frameworks/glossary skills on demand (audit). Applies to both governance and USO/PSO compliance.
design_principles.scope: Applies to governance architecture, USO/PSO compliance, and every harness capability.

design_principles.label: Ambiguity is a defect
design_principles.statement: If a rule, reference, or plan can be read two ways, that is a bug. Surface it immediately via /incident skill per incident-governance.md. Every session has this duty.
design_principles.evidence: Governed vocabulary with 134+ terms (glossary.json). Incident governance framework with structured filing process. Surfacing duty is continuous, not periodic.
design_principles.scope: Applies universally — rules, references, plans, code, and terminology.

design_principles.label: Full context, not token budgeting
design_principles.statement: Use the full context window. Launch subagents with complete rules. Load reference files generously. Keep CLAUDE.md and rules succinct for clarity, not to save tokens.
design_principles.evidence: CLAUDE.md and rules use @-references for depth. Subagent prompts inject critical rules. Skills and reference files provide depth without burdening CLAUDE.md.
design_principles.scope: Applies to every session, every subagent launch, every reference load decision.

design_principles.label: Specs vs state
design_principles.statement: Rules and references define what SHOULD be. The /incident skill tracks what IS NOT yet. Never describe a feature as 'working' if it hasn't fired in production.
design_principles.evidence: Incident governance framework distinguishes spec deviation from planned features. Code-correct vs operationally-verified distinction enforced in script-standards.md.
design_principles.scope: Applies to all harness capabilities, features, and hooks.

design_principles.label: Process discipline as work product
design_principles.statement: The observation-to-fact pipeline — observe, classify against governed vocabulary, verify against evidence, correct — IS the primary deliverable of every session. Code changes are outputs of the discipline, not substitutes for it.
design_principles.evidence: Added to CLAUDE.md by session 77a33baf (commit 9faa943). Running estimate, operational learning, and structured observations are primary session artifacts. Framework adoption pending.
design_principles.scope: Applies to every session, every platform, every aitools developer.

design_principles.label: Recency weight
design_principles.statement: Most recent instruction wins. Read conversation chronologically (oldest first). The latest turn overrides all prior guidance on the same topic.
design_principles.notes: Operative (not yet codified as rule or hook). Applies to instruction conflict resolution within sessions.
design_principles.codification_status: Pending — candidate for framework adoption as part of context rot mitigation.

design_principles.label: Treat static files as assumptions
design_principles.statement: Everything in files may be stale. Context (conversation, recent tool output) overrides file content. Verify file state before acting on it.
design_principles.notes: Operative (not yet codified as rule or hook). Related to context rot mitigation framework proposal.
design_principles.codification_status: Pending — candidate for context rot mitigation framework.

design_principles.label: Verify, don't infer
design_principles.statement: Check before assuming. Do not report a state as fact without verifying it with a tool call or concrete evidence. 'I believe X is the case' is not verification.
design_principles.notes: Operative (not yet codified as rule or hook). Surfaced from session observation: agent reported 'YES files in context' without verifying.
design_principles.codification_status: Pending — candidate for process discipline framework.

design_principles.label: Disciplined initiative
design_principles.statement: Auftragstaktik: mission-type orders, initiative within mission boundaries, escalation when scope is unclear. Agents execute the commander's intent, not literal orders when intent is clear.
design_principles.notes: Operative (not yet codified as rule). Governed vocabulary includes Auftrag, Mitdenken, Reibung, Schwerpunkt, Lagebeurteilung.
design_principles.codification_status: Pending — candidate for orchestration patterns framework.

design_principles.label: Own what matters, rent what doesn't
design_principles.statement: Own governance, lifecycle management, and orchestration. Rent the LLM platform (Claude, GPT, etc.). The harness must not be coupled to a specific model.
design_principles.notes: Operative (not yet codified as rule). Manifests in invoke_ai/Invoke-AI speed tiers using model-agnostic names, not hardcoded model identifiers.

design_principles.label: Separate tool harnesses
design_principles.statement: Claude Code (.claude/rules/, CLAUDE.md) and Cursor (.cursor/rules/, agents.md) serve different purposes and are managed independently. No parity requirement.
design_principles.evidence: Separate rule directories, separate skip CI/CD, separate check scripts. Cross-platform awareness governs both without mandating identical content.
design_principles.scope: Applies to harness architecture and maintenance decisions.

design_principles.label: End users are developers
design_principles.statement: No 'dumb user' persona. Skills, docs, and menus assume developer familiarity. Users may work on one, two, or all three platforms — aitools supports all combinations.
design_principles.evidence: Skills expose internals. Check scripts show structured output. Reference files include code patterns. No wizard-style abstractions that hide complexity.
design_principles.scope: Applies to all user-facing skills, docs, menus, and error messages.

design_principles.label: Skills as enablement
design_principles.statement: Every managed tool, dependency, and repeatable process gets a skill. Every skill with auto-trigger behavior requires three artifacts: the skill itself, a trigger directive in its governing rule, and a detection hook spec.
design_principles.evidence: 18 skills deployed (9 project, 9 user). Trigger directives in frameworks.md, glossary.md, governed-data-access.md, tool-ops.md, incident-governance.md. Hook specs in governance-and-compliance-framework.md.
design_principles.scope: Applies to every skill with auto-trigger behavior.

design_principles.label: Document intent
design_principles.statement: Every markdown file, every major section, and every code file must state its intent: purpose (what it exists to deliver), scope (what's covered and excluded), and audience (who consumes it). Intent is a protected activity — draft and present for user approval before writing.
design_principles.evidence: Intent blocks present in rules/*.md, reference/*.md, CLAUDE.md. Intent-writing and intent-audit skills deployed. Sources-of-truth.md lists intent statements as always-protected.
design_principles.scope: Applies to all new files and incrementally to existing files.

summary.purpose: Prevention layer of three-layer governance. Always in context. Define what SHOULD be.

entries.name: agentic-standards
entries.purpose: Governs all AI CLI invocations in reusable scripts. Ensures structured prompts, validated outputs, logged telemetry, and tiered speed/permission escalation.
key_directives: All AI CLI invocations in reusable scripts must use invoke_ai / Invoke-AI from aitools-lib
Speed tiers: fast (haiku/simple), balanced (sonnet/moderate), quality (opus/complex). Never hardcode model names.
Permission tiers: none (default), readonly, full, dangerous (requires explicit justification)
Every prompt must follow structured pattern: Role, Context, Task, Constraints, Output format
Every AI invocation must log structured telemetry to deploy.log: speed tier, backend, validation result, retry count
User-facing AI invocations must show transparency (backend, tier, purpose) and progress spinner for >3 second operations
Prompts must be self-contained — never reference file paths when tool use is disabled

entries.name: aitools-workspace
entries.purpose: Governs the .aitools/ workspace namespace — project-scoped harness capabilities that persist across sessions and machines. Ensures cross-machine carry-forward via git.
key_directives: Workspace structure: scratch/ (gitignored), channel/session-*/ (gitignored), channel/running-estimate.json (tracked), channel/handoffs/ (tracked), harvesting/ (tracked)
Cross-machine carry-forward: state that must survive machine switches must be tracked in git
Session-ephemeral data (scratch files, in-flight channel messages) is gitignored
Scope boundary: project-scoped (.aitools/) for project data, user-scoped (~/.aitools/) for identity/credentials/telemetry. These never mix.

entries.name: artifact-harvesting
entries.purpose: Governs the lifecycle of reusable artifacts produced during sessions. Ensures artifacts are harvested, evaluated, and either promoted into the harness or pruned.
key_directives: MUST harvest at session end: code, prompts, research, patterns from .scratch/ that represent reusable work
MUST NOT harvest: commit message files, build/check logs, temp output captures, files already committed
Auto-prune when ALL true: age >30 days, zero git references, not flagged 'keep', status still 'harvested'
Promotion candidates when ANY true: referenced in git log, manually flagged, age >7 days AND similar pattern in harness inventory
SessionEnd hook: classify .scratch/, harvest artifacts, delete ephemeral files, ship KPIs
SessionStart hook: audit harvesting/, auto-prune stale, log candidates, ship inventory KPIs

entries.name: config-file-safety
entries.purpose: Governs safe handling of JSON configuration files — read-then-merge pattern, managed vs preserved field distinction, backup before write, post-write validation.
key_directives: Always read existing config before writing — never overwrite with defaults
Distinguish managed fields (script controls) from preserved fields (user owns, never touched)
Backup before every write using backup_file / Backup-File from aitools-lib
Post-write validation: parse JSON, verify managed fields landed, log result
JSON field-level review for interactive deployments: show only managed fields that differ

entries.name: cross-platform
entries.purpose: Governs cross-platform scripting — both .sh and .ps1 for every setup script, OS guards, uname -s dispatch for hooks, and known command divergences between macOS (BSD) and Linux/Git Bash (GNU).
key_directives: Every setup/utility script gets both .sh and .ps1 variants unless listed in exemptions table
OS guards are mandatory: PS1 checks $IsWindows, bash checks uname -s
Guards MUST use structured logging — source init-logging before the guard
NEVER use stat -f || stat -c fallback chain in hooks — GNU stat -f means --file-system on Git Bash, causes silent wrong results
Canonical stat dispatch: uname -s dispatch with explicit Darwin vs other branch
Known divergences: stat, find, grep -P, date parsing — all require uname -s dispatch
Dead code rule: no platform branches for rejected platform below an OS guard
PowerShell 7 (pwsh) is the project baseline

entries.name: deploy-paths
entries.purpose: Governs the two deployment paths: scripts/ (dev path, sources aitools-lib) and deploy/ (MDM path, self-contained generated scripts). Both must produce equivalent results.
key_directives: scripts/ path: sources aitools-lib.sh/.ps1 at runtime
deploy/ path: aitools-lib inlined by build-deploy.sh at build time. No runtime repo dependency.
Both paths must produce functionally equivalent results
deploy/ is 100% generated — uncommitted changes are ephemeral (see git-safety.md)

entries.name: documentation-standards
entries.purpose: Governs documentation format — RELEASE_NOTES structure, ROADMAP format, and the layered reference architecture where rules are brief and reference files are detailed.
key_directives: RELEASE_NOTES: versioned entries with date, summary, changes grouped by category
ROADMAP: items with status, priority, brief description, linked plans
Layered architecture: rules state governance briefly, reference files provide implementation detail
@-references in rules point to reference files — agents load depth on demand

entries.name: frameworks
entries.purpose: Governs how the harness grows — agents check existing frameworks before assuming, and new frameworks follow the adoption lifecycle. Provides trigger directive for /frameworks skill.
key_directives: Governing principle: check whether an existing framework addresses a decision point before assuming. The assumption is the failure mode.
Three-layer registry pattern: rule (governance) + JSON (data, source of truth) + skill (access layer). Always.

Invoke /frameworks skill when: checking if framework exists, looking up implementing artifacts, checking provenance, adding newly adopted framework, discussing framework governance, user says /frameworks

entries.name: git-safety
entries.purpose: Governs safe git operations — deploy/ is ephemeral and safe to reset, scripts/ is source and must never be bulk-reset. Pre-pull reset scope is strictly limited.
key_directives: deploy/ is 100% generated by build-deploy.sh — uncommitted changes do not survive aitools run
scripts/ is source — the pre-pull reset must NEVER include scripts/ or any source directory
Pre-pull reset scope rule: only include directories that are fully generated (currently: deploy/ only)
When adding a new directory to pre-pull reset: document WHY in code comment and in this rule

entries.name: glossary
entries.purpose: Lists all governed terms, base artifacts, and scope modifiers so agents always have them in context. Provides trigger directive for /glossary skill.
key_directives: Lists all governed terms (134+) including scope modifiers, base artifacts, operational terms (Auftrag, Mitdenken, etc.)

Invoke /glossary skill (not raw JSON) when: checking if term is governed, discussing naming, resolving terminology ambiguity, adding governed term, user mentions glossary or asks 'what should we call X?'
Definitions and composition: use /glossary skill, not direct JSON access

entries.name: governed-data-access
entries.purpose: Governs how governed JSON registries are accessed — skill-gated only, never direct. A JSON path in a non-skill file is a bypass vector.
key_directives: Governed JSON files are accessed ONLY through their governing skill
What MAY reference JSON paths: governing skill's SKILL.md, programmatic artifacts (scripts, hooks, tests), the JSON file's own meta section
What MUST NOT reference JSON paths: .claude/rules/*.md, CLAUDE.md, reference/*.md, .cursor/rules/*.mdc, plans/
Enforcement: prevention (this rule), detection (pre-commit step 16 capability bypass audit)

entries.name: hook-rollout
entries.purpose: Governs safe hook deployment — observe-then-enforce pattern. Pre-deploy: syntax check, smoke test, violation test. Per-check mode variables for controlled rollout.
key_directives: Observe-then-enforce: hooks start in observe mode, graduate to enforce mode after verification
Pre-deploy checks: syntax validation, smoke test (fires correctly), violation test (catches what it should)
Per-check mode variables: each hook check has its own mode variable for granular control
Never deploy a hook that hasn't been smoke-tested

entries.name: incident-governance
entries.purpose: Governs how harness deficiencies are filed, classified, tracked, and resolved. Defines the surfacing duty as continuous and non-negotiable.
key_directives: Files three types: spec deviation, ambiguity, operational incident

Required fields: id, title, status, severity, affected, linked, referenceFile, observation, expected, impact, discoveryContext, discipline, frameworks, suggestedResolution, rootCause, correctiveAction, preventionLayer, created, updated
Severity: critical (deployment/data loss/security), high (silent wrong behavior/rule violations), medium (documentation drift), low (cleanup/style)
Lifecycle: open → planned → closed. No 'in progress' state.
Surfacing duty: continuous — every planning and coding session actively looks for deficiencies
Ambiguity routing: terminological → /glossary skill. Structural → /incident skill.
Staleness: incidents open >90 days without linked plan are stale

entries.name: interactive-menus
entries.purpose: Governs interactive deployment menus — cross-platform parity, console I/O patterns, JSON field-level review, and the overwrite/adopt/skip/abort state machine.
key_directives: PS1 and bash menus MUST show identical options in identical order
Every return value from Deploy-ManagedFile / deploy_managed_file MUST be handled at every call site
Non-interactive fallback: AITOOLS_FORCE env var or non-terminal stdin → auto-select overwrite
PS1 console I/O: [Console]::ReadLine() / [Console]::WriteLine() — NOT Read-Host or Write-Host
Bash console I/O: read -r < /dev/tty / printf ... > /dev/tty — NOT bare read
PS1 encoding: read external command output via temp file + [IO.File]::ReadAllText UTF8 — never pipeline
JSON field-level review: show only managed fields that differ. Adopt option only for profile.json-sourced fields.

entries.name: managed-file-deployment
entries.purpose: Governs the three deployment types — Markdown, JSON config, Shell script — with shared requirements: backup, diff logging, validation, and three-outcome tracking.
key_directives: Three deployment types: Markdown (text diff review), JSON config (field-level review), Shell script (text diff review)
Shared requirements for all types: backup before write, log diff to deploy.log, validate after write, track three outcomes (unchanged/updated/failed)
Deploy-ManagedFile / deploy_managed_file is the access point — never bypass with direct file writes for managed files

entries.name: plan-execution
entries.purpose: Governs execution of large plans — sub-agent pattern prevents rule fade during long sessions. Plans modifying 3+ files or any shared library file must use this pattern.
key_directives: Threshold: plans modifying 3+ code files OR any shared library file → sub-agent execution required
Sub-agent pattern: verbatim code in plan, error-handling audit per block, fresh sub-agent per batch with rules injected, main agent verification between batches
Sub-agent prompts must inject the error-handling rules block from reference/plan-execution-detail.md
Below threshold (1-2 files, no lib changes): direct execution OK but error-handling audit step still required

entries.name: script-standards
entries.purpose: Governs all reusable scripts — block order, error tracking, log format, external command handling, build prerequisite validation, and exit footer requirements.
key_directives: Bash block order: shebang+header, set -euo pipefail, source aitools-lib.sh + logging_init, OS guard, body, exit footer
PS1 block order: header, . aitools-lib.ps1 + Initialize-Logging, OS guard, body, exit footer
log_error MUST increment ERRORS; log_warn MUST increment WARNINGS — missing tracking is a bug
Log line format: [timestamp] [script-name] [level] message. UTC timestamps with Z suffix.
Cross-platform grep: NEVER use grep -P (macOS BSD grep doesn't support it). Use perl -ne or grep -E.
External install commands: capture output, check exit codes, distinguish 'up to date' from failure
KnownPaths: all entries must be empirically verified on actual platform. Unverified → marked # UNVERIFIED.
Every setup script must call write_summary / Write-Summary for every code path (success AND failure)
Error suppression patterns (SilentlyContinue, 2>/dev/null, || true, try/catch) require immediate result check

entries.name: smoke-test-pattern
entries.purpose: Governs how setup scripts are run as functional smoke tests from Claude Code — output to log file, check exit code, read log only on failure.
key_directives: Redirect output to a log file — never parse setup script output inline
Check exit code — the Bash tool result shows just the exit code
Read the log only if needed — on failure or to verify specific content
Platform dispatch: pwsh -File for .ps1 on Windows, bash for .sh on macOS

entries.name: sources-of-truth
entries.purpose: Governs the source-of-truth review gate — 30+ protected files require draft-present-approve workflow before any write, edit, or delete. Intent statements are always protected.
key_directives: Protected file workflow: draft change → present for review (full content for new, diff for edits) → wait for approval → write
Exceptions: trivial fixes (typos, whitespace, no meaning change) and user-dictated content (pre-approved)
Intent statements are protected in ANY file they appear in — always require user approval

30+ protected files including: tool-registry.json, CLAUDE.md, shared/claude-shared.md, all .claude/rules/*.md, incidents.json, framework-registry.json, glossary.json, all reference/framework-*.md, plans/*.md, ROADMAP.md, tool-ops-claude-code.md

entries.name: tool-evaluation
entries.purpose: Governs tool evaluation before any install or recommendation. 8 ranked principles. All evaluations through /tool-eval skill. Health flags per platform.
key_directives: Hard blocks: unverified publisher, repo inactive 2+ years, known security advisories, personal fork when official exists, typosquatting
Yellow flags (disclose and let user decide): low adoption, sole maintainer, no release in 12+ months, excessive permissions, no license
All evaluations go through /tool-eval skill
Health flags tracked per platform in tool-registry.json

entries.name: tool-lifecycle
entries.purpose: Governs tool lifecycle phases — Phase 2 gate (hard stop after install, before integration). Onboarding checklist. Install method must come from official docs, never from assumption.
key_directives: Phase 2 gate: mandatory hard stop after successful install verification, before harness integration
Onboarding checklist: evaluate → install → verify → document in tool-registry.json → integrate
Install methods must be derived from official tool documentation via /tool-eval skill — never from assumption or memory
BuildPrereqs entries must reference official documentation as source

entries.name: tool-ops
entries.purpose: Governs per-tool operational metadata — governance modes, deny rules, hooks, context injection, and verification specs. Check ops reference before assuming any tool behavior.
key_directives: Governing principle: check the tool's ops reference before assuming how a managed tool behaves
Invoke /tool-ops skill when: checking deny rules/hooks/behavior, verifying documentation access method, adding/updating ops metadata, discussing governance modes, user says /tool-ops
Assumption about tool behavior is the failure mode — ops reference is the source of truth

entries.name: web-sources
entries.purpose: Governs when to use Chrome DevTools MCP vs WebFetch — Chrome DevTools for official docs requiring accuracy, WebFetch for general research and quick fact-checks.
key_directives: Chrome DevTools MCP for: install commands, config steps, API references — anything recorded verbatim. Handles JS-rendered content.
WebFetch for: general research, blog posts, quick fact-checks. Summarizes via smaller model, may miss JS-rendered content.
Never use WebFetch when the exact text of install commands or API references matters

summary.enforcement: Repeated violations end the working relationship (stated in CLAUDE.md). Non-negotiable.

user_standing_orders.label: Dedicated tools for file ops
user_standing_orders.statement: Use Read/Edit/Write/Grep/Glob for file operations. Bash is for shell execution only (git, scripts, build commands).

user_standing_orders.label: Investigate user-reported problems
user_standing_orders.statement: When the user reports unexpected behavior, it is real. Investigate first; do not deflect or speculate.

user_standing_orders.label: Scratch files for complex scripting
user_standing_orders.statement: Never inline long commands in the Bash tool. Write to the session scratch directory (per /scratch skill), execute. The SessionEnd hook handles cleanup. Inline only for simple one-liners.

user_standing_orders.label: Perl for string manipulation
user_standing_orders.statement: Use Perl (not sed/awk) for non-trivial string manipulation. sed is fine for trivial single substitutions only.

user_standing_orders.label: No silent failures in reusable code
user_standing_orders.statement: In any code meant to run more than once, never suppress errors without checking the result and logging/failing. Applies when: project has a logging framework, is production code, or has reliability expectations. Does NOT apply to scratch/temp/throwaway work.

user_standing_orders.label: Simple Bash commands only
user_standing_orders.statement: Never use $(...), backticks, &&, ||, ;, or glob patterns in destructive commands (rm) in Bash tool calls. For commit messages, write to session scratch and use git commit -F. For sequential commands, make separate Bash calls. Pipelines (|) are OK.

project_standing_orders.label: Checklist scripts, not ad-hoc
project_standing_orders.statement: Use the project's check scripts (check-pre-commit, check-pre-push, check-post-push) instead of ad-hoc commands. Ad-hoc is OK for novel one-off checks only.

project_standing_orders.label: Platform-native dispatch
project_standing_orders.statement: Run .ps1 via pwsh -File on Windows, .sh via bash on macOS. Never run .sh setup scripts on Windows — they skip PS1 validation and miss Windows-only issues. Exceptions: hooks (bash on all platforms) and build-deploy.sh (approved exception).

project_standing_orders.label: Equal platform visibility
project_standing_orders.statement: When showing usage examples, commands, or invocations in docs, always show both macOS/bash and Windows/PowerShell. Never abbreviate one platform as 'same but .ps1' or similar.

project_standing_orders.label: Audit broadly
project_standing_orders.statement: When auditing error handling, check both suppressed errors (SilentlyContinue, 2>/dev/null) AND missing error handling (no try/catch, no -ErrorAction, bare Get-Content on untrusted input). Pattern matching finds suppressions; 'what happens if this fails?' finds gaps.

project_standing_orders.label: Dual-script rule
project_standing_orders.statement: Every setup script gets both .sh and .ps1 with OS guards. Shell-only scripts are exceptions that must be documented in .claude/rules/cross-platform.md with rationale. Current exceptions: hooks (bash on all platforms by CC design) and build-deploy.sh.

project_standing_orders.label: Script logging
project_standing_orders.statement: All deploy, setup, check and all other reusable scripts use structured logging — log/log_ok/log_error/log_warn (bash) and Log/LogOk/LogError/LogWarn (PS1). Never suggest, plan nor implement reusable scripts without structured logging.

project_standing_orders.label: Sub-agent execution for large plans
project_standing_orders.statement: Plans modifying 3+ code files (or any shared library) must use the sub-agent execution pattern: verbatim code in plan, error-handling audit per block, fresh sub-agent per batch with rules injected, main agent verification between batches.

project_standing_orders.label: Fail, don't mask
project_standing_orders.statement: Never mask broken states with fallbacks. If a managed dependency (tool, config, path) is missing or misconfigured, that is a failure — surface it via log_error / LogError and exit. Do not silently fall back to bundled, unmanaged, or degraded alternatives.

decisions.statement: NEVER use stat -f %m "$file" || stat -c %Y "$file" fallback chain pattern. On Git Bash, GNU stat -f means --file-system (not format), partially succeeds with wrong multiline output, contaminating the variable. Under set -u, bash arithmetic crashes. Use uname -s dispatch instead.

hooks.summary: 11 hooks form the detection layer backbone. They enforce standing orders, manage session lifecycle, maintain the dashboard, guard governed data access, and audit tool operations. All hooks are pure bash, portable across macOS/Linux/Windows Git Bash, and deployed to ~/.claude/hooks/ by setup-user-hooks.sh.

inventory.purpose: Block the built-in claude-code-guide subagent (Haiku model) which returns inaccurate hook type schemas. Caused incident #34730 where all hooks were disabled.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Agent receives corrective context: correct hook type schemas (command requires command, prompt requires prompt, http requires url, agent requires prompt), CC docs URLs at code.claude.com/docs/en/*.md. Prevents schema confusion that leads to broken settings.json.
inventory.implementation: Pure bash regex extracts subagent_type from JSON stdin. Returns JSON deny with permissionDecisionReason containing corrective knowledge. All other agent types pass through (exit 0, no output).

inventory.purpose: Auto-launch live dashboard server in background at session start.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Dashboard available at http://localhost:8411 within seconds. If already running (PID alive), skips silently. User gets live view of running estimate state.
inventory.implementation: Thin dispatcher: extracts cwd from hook input, finds project root (git rev-parse), locates aitools CLI (PATH then ~/.local/bin/aitools). Delegates to 'aitools dashboard --background'. Fallback: direct Python launch of generate-dashboard.py --serve if CLI not installed. Searches for estimate in .aitools/channel/ then .scratch/session-*/. PID file at .aitools/.dashboard-pid. Default port 8411.

inventory.purpose: Turn counting + Lagebeurteilung reminder at context growth thresholds + estimate staleness check.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Agent receives periodic reminders via stderr to update running estimate. At turn 15 and every 15 turns: structured Lagebeurteilung reminder naming fields to refresh. If estimate file mtime >30 min stale: staleness warning. Drives the auto-refresh cycle: agent updates estimate -> mtime changes -> server watcher detects -> HTML regenerated -> browser polls and re-renders.
inventory.implementation: Marker directory in /tmp/aitools-estimate-<session_id>. Turn count in turn-count file, incremented each invocation. Last Lagebeurteilung turn tracked in last-lage-turn file. Estimate freshness: finds estimate file (same search as dashboard-serve), gets mtime via uname -s dispatch (Darwin: stat -f %m, else: stat -c %Y). NEVER uses fallback chain pattern.

inventory.purpose: Detect direct access to glossary.json/glossary.md and remind agent to use /glossary skill.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Soft reminder via stderr additionalContext. Does not block. Enforces governed data access pattern: skills gate JSON registries.
inventory.implementation: Extracts file_path from stdin JSON via perl regex. Case match on *glossary.json or *glossary.md. Returns additionalContext JSON on match. Exit 0 always.

inventory.purpose: Classify session scratch contents and harvest artifacts. Route handoffs. Update manifest.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Reusable artifacts (code, scripts, research, patterns) automatically preserved in harvesting/ with date+session naming. Ephemeral files (logs, commit messages, tmp) skipped. Handoff files routed to .aitools/channel/handoffs/. Manifest updated for next session's audit. Session directory NOT deleted (30-file loss incident lesson).
inventory.implementation: Pure bash JSON field extraction (grep+sed). Classification by file extension: .py/.sh/.ps1/.js/.ts = artifact, .log/.tmp/commit-msg* = ephemeral, .json (non-config) = artifact, .md (non-log) = artifact. Handoff routing: files matching handoff* go to .aitools/channel/handoffs/. Manifest update via Node.js (available via managed Node). Auto-creates harvesting/ on first harvest. Stale pruning: marks artifacts >30 days old with zero git refs as 'pruned' in manifest (does NOT delete files). Counter collision avoidance with incrementing suffix.
inventory.designDecision: No auto-delete of session dir. Previously rm -rf'd the dir, but 30 files were lost when harvest partially failed in session Z1IhGrcgGO (2026-03-21). Now dirs accumulate in .scratch/ and scratch-init.sh logs stale ones.

inventory.purpose: Create deterministic session scratch directory. Log stale dirs. Discover handoffs.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Agent sees session dir path in context (stdout). Stale dirs logged (not deleted). Handoff files announced if found. Enables agent to use .scratch/session-<id>/ for all temp files.
inventory.implementation: Extracts session_id from hook input JSON. Deterministic dir name: .scratch/session-<first 10 chars of session_id>. Falls back to mktemp if session_id empty. Writes path to .scratch/.current-session. Stale detection: find -maxdepth 1 -name 'session-*' -mmin +1440. Handoff discovery: iterates .aitools/channel/handoffs/handoff* files.

inventory.purpose: Copy session transcript to user's dotprofile repo for archival.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Transcripts accumulate in aitools-<username>/sessions/<project>/. Enables cross-session analysis. No git operations — copy only.
inventory.implementation: Reads session_id, cwd, transcript_path from hook input. Reads userRepoPath from ~/.aitools/config.json. Derives project name from git remote or cwd basename. Date from transcript file birth time (platform dispatch: Darwin stat -f '%SB', else stat -c %W with mtime fallback). Copies to <userRepoPath>/sessions/<project>/YYYY-MM-DD_<prefix>.jsonl. Skips if already archived.

inventory.purpose: Auto-fix .sh files: CRLF->LF, chmod +x, git index executable bit.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Every .sh file is correct immediately after Write/Edit. No manual fixup cycle. Eliminates recurring 'bad interpreter' and 'permission denied' errors.
inventory.implementation: Extracts file_path from tool input. Only acts on *.sh files. CRLF detection via perl -ne 'exit 1 if /\r/'. CRLF fix via perl -pi -e 's/\r$//'. chmod +x on disk. Git index update: checks mode via git ls-files -s, runs git update-index --chmod=+x if 100644. Reports fixes via stderr.

inventory.purpose: Enforce USOs by inspecting Bash commands before execution.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Hard blocks prevent dangerous USO violations. Advisory observations logged for non-enforced patterns. Reduces permission prompt storms and accidental data loss.
inventory.implementation: Per-check mode variables: MODE_AND=enforce, MODE_SUBSHELL=enforce, MODE_SCRATCH=enforce, MODE_REST=observe. violation() helper dispatches based on mode. Checks (in order): scratch files (>4 newlines = too complex for inline, ENFORCE), compound operators (&& ENFORCE, || observe, ; observe with pwsh/perl exemption), $() ENFORCE, backticks observe, dedicated tool bypass (cat/head/tail/grep/find/sed/awk observed, pipeline exemption), glob in rm. First-token allowlist: pwsh, git, npm, node, python*, pip*, cargo, brew etc pass through.

inventory.purpose: Periodic surfacing duty reminder + incident-acknowledgment detection.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Agent reminded every 30 min to look for incidents/ambiguities. If agent says 'incident' or 'pre-existing' without filing, receives targeted reminder to invoke /incident or leave TODO(incident): marker.
inventory.implementation: Marker file in /tmp/aitools-surfacing-<session_id>. Session age check via transcript birth time (uname -s dispatch for stat). Acknowledgment detection: reads last 100 lines of transcript (tail), regex for incident language patterns, checks for /incident or TODO(incident): in same chunk. Suppression: if incidents.json mtime < 1800s, suppresses (recently filed).

inventory.purpose: Run contract tests against deployed hooks. Detect drift. Check version dep staleness.
inventory.behavioralImpact: Structured audit results accumulate in tool-ops-audit.jsonl. Surfaces drift between registry and deployed state. Contract tests catch hook regressions.
inventory.implementation: Finds tool-ops.json via AITOOLS_REPO_PATH or $HOME/repos/aitools/. For block-claude-code-guide.sh: pipes mock JSON (deny test + allow test), checks output. Drift: checks if hook appears in ~/.claude/settings.json. Stale deps: greps tool-ops-claude-code.md for 'CRITICAL.*Last verified'. Emits JSONL to ~/.claude/hooks/logs/tool-ops-audit.jsonl. Always exits 0 (advisory).

dashboardSystem.overview: Live HTML dashboard for running estimates. Self-contained static mode (file:// safe) and live server mode (auto-refresh without reload). First S1 (Administration) capability in the harness.

modes.static: Default. Embeds JSON into HTML. Works from file:///. No server needed.
modes.live: --serve flag. Starts Python http.server with file watcher. Dashboard polls /api/estimate every 3s. Re-renders via DOM update without page reload.

generator.fileWatcher: os.stat polling (cross-platform, no dependencies). Checks mtime every 1s. On change: reload JSON, rebuild HTML, update server.dashboard_html.

dashboardSystem.dataFlow: Agent updates estimate JSON -> file mtime changes -> server file watcher detects (1s poll) -> regenerates served HTML -> browser polls /api/estimate (3s) -> JavaScript compares data -> DOM update without reload. End-to-end: ~4s best case, ~7s worst case.

schwerpunkt.current: SQLite migration: convert harness state from JSON files to SQLite (Python sqlite3). Multi-DB architecture: per-session DBs (.aitools/sessions/<id>.db) + harness DB (.aitools/harness.db). Option B: SQLite runtime (gitignored) + JSON archive (tracked, carries forward via git). Everything into DB. New hooks needed.
schwerpunkt.rationale: JSON files are human-readable but not queryable, not atomic, and not concurrent-safe. SQLite provides atomic writes, indexable history, and a single carry-forward artifact per project.
schwerpunkt.nextAction: Schema finalization and Phase 1 implementation (harness.db + session DB creation in hooks)

observations.text: Carry-forward pipeline structural gap: SessionEnd hook writes outputs to disk but no automation commits or pushes them. Running estimate, OL JSON, and harvested artifacts from every session remain uncommitted until manually committed. On a machine switch before manual commit, all session outputs are lost.

Cross-platform hook failures recurring: the stat -f || stat -c fallback chain anti-pattern has been introduced and discovered 4 times across sessions. Each time it is fixed on the platform where it fails; each time it reappears in new code written on the other platform. The pattern is not being suppressed at the source.

Correct patterns exist but new code uses old patterns: canonical stat dispatch is documented in cross-platform.md and used in session-archive.sh:68, yet two other hooks were written using the fallback chain pattern. Agents write from memory or from other files in context rather than checking the canonical source.

Channel infrastructure decided but never implemented: decisions #22-24 in planning-brief.json specify SITREP and FINDING channel files. Zero SITREPs and zero FINDINGs have ever been written. The infrastructure exists in the design but not in the hooks or scripts.

Dashboard 'ship' miss: generate-dashboard.py was committed and described as shipped in session 5HyCwPtSDH, but the aitools-dashboard.sh/.ps1 wrapper scripts were not verified to actually produce rendered HTML. The capability was described as done when it was only partially implemented.

Namespace consolidation gap: decision #34 specifies .aitools/scratch/ and .aitools/harvesting/ but hooks still reference .scratch/ and harvesting/ at repo root. The decision was made but implementation did not propagate to the hooks.

Context rot on commander intent: in session RnTOD5XJFi, after 10+ intelligence missions, the agent lost track of the commander's original intent (populate harness-state.json) and was generating outputs that did not serve that goal. Re-reading the commander's framing recovered direction.

Behavioral framing gap in /resume: the /aitool-resume RFC describes what to include in a resume prompt but not how to weight it behaviorally. Agents that receive a resume prompt treat it as informational, not as a binding behavioral directive. Presence in context is not behavioral weight.

Assumption propagation without verification: multiple claims in running estimates were stated as facts that were actually assumptions (e.g., 'all stat instances fixed', 'dashboard is operational'). These propagated into subsequent sessions without challenge.

Demonstrate-then-skip at subsequent transitions: a pattern demonstrated once (e.g., check pre-commit before committing, read commander framing before acting) is performed in the session where it is introduced, then skipped in subsequent sessions. The demonstration creates the appearance of an established pattern when it is actually a one-time event.

Subagent cross-repo file access restriction: subagents launched from the aitools repo cannot read files in dotprofile repos (~/repos/aitools-nobul-jose/) without explicit path inclusion in the delegation prompt. This is a security boundary, not a bug, but it caused mission failures when subagents assumed they could read user-level files.

Subagent cross-repo file access restriction (confirmed): subagents do not inherit the parent session's working directory or file access context. Delegations that require reading files from repos other than the current working directory must include explicit absolute paths or file content inline in the delegation prompt.

insights.text: Commit gap: the SessionEnd hook is not the end of the carry-forward pipeline. The pipeline has at least 6 stages: (1) write outputs, (2) classify artifacts, (3) update running estimate, (4) git add, (5) git commit, (6) git push. The hook covers stage 1-2. Stages 4-6 are manual and frequently skipped, breaking carry-forward.

No detection layer for platform portability: the three-layer governance model (Prevention/Detection/Audit) has a gap at the Detection layer for cross-platform patterns. The stat fallback chain anti-pattern has no hook or check script step that fires when new code introduces it. Prevention (documentation) is insufficient without Detection.

Decided ≠ Implemented: the harness has a systematic gap between design decisions and implementation verification. Channel (#22-24), namespace consolidation (#34), auto-commit (#1), and multiple other decisions exist in planning-brief.json but have no implementation verification step. A decision without a verification gate is aspirational, not operational.

Audit shipped capabilities, not shipped decisions: the dashboard miss demonstrates that 'committed' ≠ 'operational'. The correct audit question is 'does this capability produce the expected output when invoked?' not 'is the code committed?'. Every claimed capability needs a smoke test.

UCIs alone do not change behavior: every recurring pattern (stat fallback chain, demonstrate-then-skip, assumption propagation) has been documented in CLAUDE.md as a UCI. None has been eliminated by the UCI alone. Only structural fixes — hooks that fire when the pattern occurs, check scripts that fail on the pattern, or canonical implementations that remove the decision point — break recurring patterns.

Mark-or-verify as a session discipline: the distinction between verified facts and assumptions must be explicit in every state document. An unverified assumption that propagates across sessions becomes a false ground truth. The discipline is: read the file (verify) or explicitly label ASSUMPTION. There is no third option.

6-stage carry-forward pipeline: carry-forward is not a single action (commit). The full pipeline is: (1) write session outputs, (2) classify artifacts for harvesting, (3) update running estimate / harness-state, (4) git add specific files, (5) git commit with structured message, (6) git push to remote. Every stage is a potential break point. The pipeline must be automated or explicitly checked at session end.

Carry-forward is session-to-session, not machine-to-machine: the fundamental unit of carry-forward is the session boundary, not the machine boundary. Machine switches are just session boundaries that happen to cross machines. The carry-forward pipeline must be complete at every session end, regardless of whether a machine switch is planned.

proposals.title: Pre-commit hook for stat pattern detection
proposals.text: Add a pre-commit hook (or check-pre-commit.sh step) that scans all modified hook files for 'stat -f' patterns not wrapped in a uname -s dispatch. Fail the commit if the forbidden pattern is detected.
proposals.barrierAnalysis: Barrier: pattern detection requires grep over hook files. Countermeasure: check-pre-commit.sh step 31 (proposed) scans shared/hooks/*.sh for stat -f without uname. Residual risk: pattern could appear in non-hook scripts not covered by the step.

proposals.title: Intent sentinel Stop hook deployment
proposals.text: Deploy the intent sentinel Stop hook designed in KHGOmVeNNM. The hook reads the session's first human message (commander framing) and compares it against the last 3 tool calls. If drift is detected, it outputs a reminder via stderr.
proposals.barrierAnalysis: Barrier: Stop hooks must use type: command, not type: prompt. The design in intent-sentinel-design.md uses type: command with stderr output — this is correct. Countermeasure: design already validated against CC hook architecture. Residual risk: drift detection heuristic may produce false positives in long research sessions.

proposals.title: SessionEnd hook carry-forward pipeline completion
proposals.text: Extend the SessionEnd hook to complete all 6 stages of the carry-forward pipeline: write outputs (stage 1-2, existing), update harness-state.json (stage 3), git add tracked files (stage 4), git commit with structured message (stage 5), git push (stage 6). The hook should fail loudly if any stage fails.
proposals.barrierAnalysis: Barrier: git commit requires a commit message. Auto-generated messages are low quality. Countermeasure: use a structured template ('SessionEnd: <session-id> <date> [<files changed>]'). Residual risk: push may fail on merge conflicts. If push fails, the hook must log the failure and leave staged changes for manual resolution.

proposals.title: Decision verification gate in planning-brief.json
proposals.text: Add a 'verificationStatus' field to every decision entry in planning-brief.json: 'decided', 'implemented', 'verified'. The /audit skill scans for decisions with verificationStatus='decided' older than 7 days and surfaces them as gaps.
proposals.barrierAnalysis: Barrier: planning-brief.json has 54 decisions; retrofitting is labor-intensive. Countermeasure: apply only to new decisions; backfill incrementally. Residual risk: the /audit skill must be updated to read the new field — currently it does not.

proposals.title: harness-state.json as session prompt source
proposals.text: harness-state.json (4-pillar artifact) is generated at session end and injected into the next session's context via SessionStart hook. This closes the bootstrap gap: agents start with full harness awareness, not partial context from running estimate.
proposals.barrierAnalysis: Barrier: harness-state.json must be populated before it can be injected. Countermeasure: this generation task (current) populates Pillars 3+4; Pillars 1+2 are populated from existing governed files. Residual risk: JSON injection into session context may hit token limits for large harness states. Mitigation: generate a compressed 'prompt-ready' version alongside the full JSON.

metaLessons.lesson: UCIs are ineffective for recurring patterns
metaLessons.detail: User Coaching Items documented in CLAUDE.md do not prevent recurrence of behavioral patterns. Only structural fixes work: hooks that fire when the pattern occurs, check scripts that fail on detection, or implementations that remove the decision point entirely. When a pattern recurs after a UCI is filed, the correct response is to design a structural fix, not to file another UCI.

Processing files larger than ~30K tokens requires chunking. Attempting to read and process a large file in a single pass causes rule fade — rules in context are ignored. Process in 2-3 file chunks with verification between each chunk.

metaLessons.lesson: Never use Explore agents — always general-purpose with write permissions
metaLessons.detail: Explore-type agents cannot write files. Any research task that might produce an artifact (a finding, a structured output, a file) must be delegated to a general-purpose agent with write permissions. Switching mid-task from Explore to Write loses context.

metaLessons.lesson: Subagents inherit NOTHING — every delegation includes full context
metaLessons.detail: Subagents launched via Task do not inherit project rules, CLAUDE.md, cross-platform rules, or harness awareness. Every delegation must include: (1) relevant rules verbatim, (2) canonical patterns for the task, (3) expected output format, (4) what NOT to do. A delegation without injected context will produce rule-unaware output.

The 1M token context window means there is no legitimate reason to truncate or summarize harness files to save context. Load them fully. The cost of full context is zero compared to the cost of missing information.

When launching multiple subagents for independent research tasks, launch them in parallel in a single message. Sequential launch wastes wall-clock time proportional to the number of tasks. Parallel launch completes in the time of the slowest task.

metaLessons.lesson: Re-read before acting — commander's most repeated instruction
metaLessons.detail: The single most repeated correction across all sessions: re-read the commander's framing before acting. Agents consistently act on their interpretation of the intent rather than the stated intent. The fix is mechanical: re-read the original message, quote the key phrase, confirm the action serves it.

metaLessons.lesson: Audit shipped capabilities — check CODE, not just DECISIONS
metaLessons.detail: A committed decision is not a shipped capability. The correct audit question is: 'Can I invoke this capability right now and get the expected output?' Checking planning-brief.json for a decision marked 'complete' does not answer this question. Read the script, run it (or trace its execution mentally), verify the output.

metaLessons.lesson: Dashboard miss meta-lesson: check scripts/ and shared/hooks/
metaLessons.detail: When investigating a capability miss, the first places to check are scripts/ and shared/hooks/ — not planning-brief.json or the running estimate. The running estimate tells you what was decided; the scripts directory tells you what was implemented.

metaLessons.lesson: Assumption propagation — verify every fact, mark unverifiable as ASSUMPTION
metaLessons.detail: Every fact in a state document that has not been verified by reading a file or running a command must be labeled ASSUMPTION. Unlabeled assumptions propagate across sessions and become false ground truth. The discipline is binary: verified or ASSUMPTION. There is no 'probably true'.

metaLessons.lesson: The file IS the harness — every word has behavioral consequences
metaLessons.detail: CLAUDE.md, rules files, harness-state.json, and operational learning are not documentation. They are behavioral directives that govern every future session. A word added carelessly propagates into agent behavior. A word omitted creates a governance gap. Every edit to a harness file is a behavioral change.

vocabularyFindings.finding: Used in two senses: (1) the session-to-session transfer of state via git (machine-agnostic), and (2) the specific 6-stage pipeline for achieving that transfer. The ambiguity creates confusion when discussing 'carry-forward gaps' — it is unclear whether the gap is in the state content or in the pipeline mechanics.
vocabularyFindings.proposedResolution: carry-forward (noun): the state that must survive a session boundary. carry-forward pipeline (noun): the 6-stage process for achieving it. The ambiguity is eliminated by always pairing 'pipeline' with the process sense.

vocabularyFindings.finding: Used loosely to mean 'the authoritative source'. The harness has multiple sources of truth (planning-brief.json for decisions, operational-learning.json for patterns, harness-state.json for consolidated state). 'Ground truth' without qualification is ambiguous.
vocabularyFindings.proposedResolution: Replace with specific artifact names. 'planning-brief.json is the decision record' not 'planning-brief.json is the ground truth'.

vocabularyFindings.finding: New term coined in OL v3 to describe the specific failure where session outputs are written but never committed. Distinct from 'carry-forward gap' (which could be any of the 6 pipeline stages). 'Commit gap' names stages 4-5 specifically.
vocabularyFindings.proposedResolution: Add to glossary as a governed term: commit gap — the condition where session outputs are written to disk but not committed to git, breaking the carry-forward pipeline at stages 4-5.

vocabularyFindings.finding: Used to mean three different things: (1) the aitools repo, (2) the dotprofile repo (aitools-nobul-jose), (3) any project repo that aitools manages. Unqualified 'repo' in instructions causes delegation failures when subagents read the wrong repo.
vocabularyFindings.proposedResolution: Always qualify: 'aitools repo', 'dotprofile repo', 'project repo'. Never use bare 'repo' in delegation prompts or harness-state entries.

vocabularyFindings.finding: New term from OL v3 session. Describes the degree to which a configuration file reflects verified current state vs. assumed state. A configuration with low confidence has unverified assumptions. A configuration with high confidence has been verified against live system state.
vocabularyFindings.proposedResolution: Add to glossary. Use in harness-state and running estimate to signal verification level of each state section.

vocabularyFindings.finding: Term considered for use in the harness to describe decision alternatives. Determined unnecessary — the harness already uses 'proposal' (in operational learning) and 'option' (in RFC language). Adding COA would introduce a fourth synonym for the same concept.
vocabularyFindings.proposedResolution: Do not adopt COA as a governed term. Use 'proposal' for OL recommendations, 'option' for RFC alternatives, 'decision' for resolved choices.

vocabularyFindings.finding: New term from OL v3. Describes the class of gaps where a lifecycle transition (session end, machine switch, decision-to-implementation) lacks automation or verification. The commit gap is an instance. The decided-not-implemented gap is another. 'Lifecycle boundary gap' is the general pattern.
vocabularyFindings.proposedResolution: Add to glossary as a governed term: lifecycle boundary gap — a class of harness deficiency where a transition between lifecycle states (session end, machine switch, decision to implementation) lacks automation or explicit verification, allowing state to be lost or to diverge silently.
